narrative:
The model predicts you have a 16% chance of failing your final year, which is why the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your number of past failures, your ambition to pursue higher education, and your record of school absences. Although you have had no previous class failures (matching the average of students who passed), the model still sees this as the strongest single factor pulling your outcome toward failure. Your clear desire to continue into higher education works in the opposite direction, pushing the prediction toward passing. However, your 22 absences stand out sharply against the average of fewer than 4 days missed by students who passed; this large gap was the third most important reason the model leaned toward failure.

Taken together, these elements created enough concern for the system to forecast a risk of not passing. To improve, you should focus immediately on attending every class, catching up on any missed material, and turning your strong motivation for higher education into a daily study habit. Even small, consistent reductions in absences and steady effort can shift your trajectory significantly before the final exams.
